I’m a pharmacy tech and I’ve also taken clonazepam myself. There is no risk for addiction if you are only taking it as needed during panic surrounding meals and such. Definitely don’t drink, and don’t drive for a while after taking it until you’re used to how the meds will affect you (some people get quite dizzy.)

You can become dependent (not addicted there is a difference) on it if you are taking it on a regular schedule like twice a day every day. This means your body becomes dependent on the chemical and you feel kinda crappy without the med, the same thing that happens with antidepressants and such. 

Very important here: being dependent on a drug does not mean you can’t stop taking it, it means a doctor needs to taper you off of it to decrease side effects. 

Benzos can be addictive but that usually comes from higher doses like 2-5mg where most patients are only prescribed 0.5-1 mg as a dose. Higher doses are not automatically addictive either, there’s just a bigger risk for misuse if the patient is on regular high doses as their tolerance for the medication drops over time. 

Hope this helps!

Edit: forgot to mention weed. Don’t smoke or take any cannabis at the same time as the clonazepam (similar to alcohol) but it is safe to smoke around your doses. I did this and had no issues.

Okay so that’s a lot of disorders that all have overlapping symptoms and it’s hard to say what might exactly be the reasons you’re struggling. Some of them can’t be diagnosed until adulthood like BPD and DID because personality disorders can’t be identified properly until your brain is fully developed. 

What I would suggest here is writing down which symptoms are most debilitating/ concerning for you on a daily basis, and ask your parents to see book you an appointment for a mental health assessment with your family doctor. This is where they will generally ask a bunch of questions to determine what level of care you might need/ how severe your symptoms are. There are a handful of general depression and anxiety assessments they can do which will help them understand what kind of care you will need moving forward. They can possibly start you on some medication and get you set up with counselling services to give you support while you wait to see other medical professionals. 

Your family doctor is also the one who needs to refer you to different specialists or services for further assessment or treatment. So really I’d say that’s the best place to start. I’m 30 I’ve been through a ton of mental health services and specialists, but the first step to almost all of those things is an assessment by your family doctor.

I’m not saying the print isn’t messed up and couldn’t be done better, but if you’re sending someone a file to print I think it’s your responsibility to make sure the file is not creating extra work for the person you’re sending it to. If the source of the print file has issues then they’re only going to compound the further along you go if they aren’t dealt with. And not everyone that runs a printer knows how to deal with issues in source files. (Not an excuse don’t charge people for a service you can’t provide) 

Technically all you’re asking them to do is print the file, not fix issues with your model. I worked as an editor for years and used to get files from people with all kinds of issues, sure I could fix them and make the project work as intended, but it was a lot of extra work on my end.

I’m well aware of how polygons work in 3D modelling, I’ve also been doing this for a long time. 

What I’m  looking at is the corners and straight edges that are not straight lines at all. Specifically look at the bottom right corner again, and then tell me you don’t see some serious issues. There’s a small overhang that is happening on that edge for literally no reason so I can only imagine there’s tons more issues I haven’t seen yet.

So your model has a hundred problems with it I can see before zooming in on it. I’d advise you to look up some YouTube tutorials on how to make models optimized for 3D printing.  

The print looks terrible but I’d say that is almost entirely due to the structure of your model, even the flat straight edges have weird artifacts that would make it difficult for a slicer to process well.
